hints: Look for the big jump in each graph, that jump tells you when you start removing an electron from a new inner shell closer to the nucleus.
The left graph jumps sharply after the 7th electron, so that element has 7 outer electrons, while the right graph jumps after the 2nd electron, so it has 2 outer electrons.
Combine a Period 3 Group 2 metal that forms a 2+ ion with a Period 3 Group 17 non-metal that forms a 1- ion, and balance the charges to get a neutral formula.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a jump means**

Think of ionisation energy as how tightly an electron is held. A small rise means same shell, a huge jump means you have broken into an inner shell.

Rule to use:
$$\text{large jump after } n \text{th IE} \rightarrow n \text{ electrons in outer shell}$$

**Identify the left element**

The left graph stays low for electrons 1 to 7, then shoots up for electron 8. That means 7 electrons are easily removed from the outer shell.

In Period 3, the element with 7 outer electrons is chlorine, $\text{Cl}$, in Group 17. It will gain 1 electron to form $\text{Cl}^{-}$.

**Identify the right element**

The right graph stays low for electrons 1 to 2, then jumps up for electron 3. That means only 2 electrons are in the outer shell.

In Period 3, the element with 2 outer electrons is magnesium, $\text{Mg}$, in Group 2. It will lose 2 electrons to form $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

**Combine to make a neutral ionic compound**

We need total positive charge = total negative charge. One $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ needs two $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ions.

$$\text{Mg}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2$$

options.A: Correct. Mg is Period 3 Group 2 with 2 valence electrons, and Cl is Period 3 Group 17 with 7 valence electrons. Mg loses 2 to give Mg2+, each Cl gains 1 to give Cl-, so two chlorides balance one magnesium to give MgCl2.
options.B: Incorrect. CaBr2 has the right 1:2 ratio and charges, but Ca is in Period 4 and Br is in Period 4. The question clearly states both elements are from Period 3, so this cannot be right.
options.C: Incorrect. Na2S would need an element with 1 outer electron (jump after 1st IE) and an element with 6 outer electrons (jump after 6th IE). Neither graph shows those patterns, so you have swapped the groups.
options.D: Incorrect. K2Se also needs a Group 1 element and a Group 16 element, which do not match the jumps after 7 and after 2. Also K and Se are in Period 4, not Period 3.
